title: Co-projection for a closed immersion
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring with a Tate twist datum, let
$i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion, let
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ and let $L$ be an *invertible* object of
$D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ (on the small étale sites). Then there is an isomorphism

$$
Ri^{!}\bigl(K\otimes^{\mathbb L}_{\Lambda_X}L\bigr)\ \cong\
Ri^{!}K\otimes^{\mathbb L}_{\Lambda_Z}Li^{*}L :
$$

an invertible tensor factor passes through $i^{!}$ at the
cost of restricting it. In particular, for $f:X\to Y$ with $f'=f\circ i$ and
$B$ invertible on $Y$, taking $L=Lf^{*}B$ and using
$Li^{*}Lf^{*}B\cong Lf'^{*}B$ gives

$$
Ri^{!}\bigl(K\otimes^{\mathbb L}_{\Lambda_X}Lf^{*}B\bigr)\ \cong\
Ri^{!}K\otimes^{\mathbb L}_{\Lambda_Z}Lf'^{*}B ;
$$

and for the Tate twists $L=\Lambda_X(m)[2m]$, whose restriction is
$\Lambda_Z(m)[2m]$, it reads
$Ri^{!}(K(m)[2m])\cong(Ri^{!}K)(m)[2m]$.
Iterating, for a separated morphism $f:X\to Y$,
$p_1,p_2:W=X\times_YX\to X$, its closed diagonal $\Delta:X\hookrightarrow W$, and $\omega_f$ invertible:

$$
R\Delta^{!}\bigl(Lp_1^{*}\omega_f\otimes^{\mathbb L}Lp_2^{*}\omega_f\bigr)
\ \cong\
\bigl(R\Delta^{!}\Lambda_W\bigr)\otimes^{\mathbb L}
L\Delta^{*}Lp_1^{*}\omega_f\otimes^{\mathbb L}L\Delta^{*}Lp_2^{*}\omega_f .
$$

All derived categories here are the ordinary unbounded categories $D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], using small representatives in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. The notation $D^b_{ctf}$ means bounded constructible complexes [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] of finite Tor amplitude [def-kun-tor-amplitude]. Derived tensor is [def-kun-derived-tensor]; $Lu^*$ is the exact constant-coefficient inverse image applied termwise [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Invertible means that there exists an object $M$ with $L\otimes^L M\cong\Lambda_T$ and $M\otimes^L L\cong\Lambda_T$. For a closed immersion $i$, $Ri^!$ denotes the right adjoint to the direct image $i_*$ on these derived categories [lem-exc-closed-ambient]. A Tate twist datum supplies invertible twist objects $\Lambda_T(m)$, inverse to $\Lambda_T(-m)$, with the specified pullback identifications $Lu^*\Lambda_T(m)\cong\Lambda_U(m)$; write $K(m)=K\otimes^L\Lambda_T(m)$. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-proper-morphism].

proof.text: A closed immersion is proper. finite_projection_iso assembles the canonical proper projection maps into an isomorphism of bifunctors. Flip its two arguments and evaluate at the inverse object M; this gives the natural isomorphism Ri*(-) tensor M ≅ Ri*(- tensor Li*M). The existing closed ambient adjoint theorem is already stated for the actual total derived direct image, so Adjunction.ofIsLeftAdjoint supplies precisely Ri* ⊣ Ri!. Apply the generic helper and evaluate at K. No boundedness or constructibility assertion about intermediate objects is required.

proof.text: For the base specialization, DerivedCategory.isInvertible.leftDerivedUpperStar pulls the inverse pair of B back along f. Apply the ambient co-projection and tensor its result with the inverse of leftDerivedUpperStarComp.app B to identify Li*Lf*B with L(i ≫ f)*B.

proof.text: For the Tate specialization, the supplied inverse identities show twist X m invertible. Its shift by 2*m is invertible by DerivedCategory.isInvertible.shift, using derivedTensorShiftIso. Apply ambient co-projection to that shifted factor. The tensor commShiftIso identifies the input with (K tensor twist X m)[2*m]; the inverse-image commShiftIso and twistPullback identify the restricted shifted factor with (twist Z m)[2*m]; the tensor commShiftIso gives the desired shifted output.

proof.text: For separated f its diagonal is closed. Both projected omega factors are invertible by monoidal pullback. Insert the inverse left unitor in the first factor and apply ambient co-projection twice, first to (unit tensor L₁) tensor L₂ and then to unit tensor L₁. Tensoring the second resulting isomorphism with the restriction of L₂ gives exactly the stated left-associated threefold tensor.

Steps 4 and 5 used them as the same functor without saying why. Every other step checks out against the statements it cites: tensor structure, inverse-tensor adjunction via quasi-inverse-adjoint, pullback of inverses, the five Hom bijections tested on all of D(Z), Yoneda, linear inverse-image composition, the even-shift Tate case, and the two-factor diagonal.
